claim_text: No public freeze-pipe damage curve exists; vendor functions are proprietary; published freeze models give no loss function.
Freezer-test times of 11.5, 6.5 and about 4.75 h at 20, 10 and 0 F are close to a constant dose (138, 143, 152 F h = 77-84 degC h); time to blockage falls roughly as 1/(32 F - T).
prohibited_inference: A threshold axis; an outdoor-air dose.

claim_text: Those doses describe the pipe's surroundings, not the outdoor air; the regional median must absorb the difference.
permitted_inference: Use 80 degC h only for the outage median and the floor.
prohibited_inference: Use 80 degC h as the heated-building median.

claim_text: The major losses from burst pipes are in the southern states because of where pipes are placed.
permitted_inference: Lower medians in warm climate zones.

claim_text: Texas losses came with accompanying power outages; outage duration should modify the curve.
prohibited_inference: A numeric outage effect from the source.

claim_text: Commercial buildings are a separate class; IBHS targets buildings north of the 32 F line.

permitted_inference: Anchor for house loss given a burst.
prohibited_inference: Read as structure-only; read as a burst frequency.
reasoning: Includes contents and other coverages, so the structure share is overstated (flag).
